subject: food-technology
topicDisplay: Being an Effective Consumer When Shopping for Food
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which date mark relates to food safety and means the food must not be eaten after that date?
questions.explain: A 'use by' date is a safety mark used on perishable foods, whereas 'best before' relates only to quality.

questions.q: How many allergens must be legally emphasised (for example in bold) within the ingredients list on UK food labels?
questions.explain: UK law requires the 14 named allergens, such as milk, eggs and peanuts, to be clearly emphasised in the ingredients list.

questions.q: In what order are ingredients listed on a food label?
questions.explain: Ingredients are listed by weight, largest first, so the main ingredient appears at the start of the list.

questions.q: The nutrition declaration on prepacked food must be given per what standard amount?
questions.explain: Giving values per 100g or 100ml allows consumers to compare different products fairly.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation QUID stand for on food labelling?
questions.explain: QUID shows the percentage of a key or named ingredient, for example the percentage of fruit in a pie.

questions.q: The reference intake (RI) for salt for an average adult is approximately how much per day?
questions.explain: The daily reference intake for salt is 6g, which helps consumers judge how much of their allowance a food provides.

questions.q: The reference intake (RI) for energy for an average adult is approximately how much per day?
questions.explain: The energy reference intake is around 2000 kcal (8400 kJ) per day for an average adult.

questions.q: Which law states that goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described?
questions.explain: The Consumer Rights Act 2015 sets out that goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described.

questions.q: Front-of-pack traffic light labelling uses colour coding for which four nutrients?
questions.explain: Traffic light labels colour code fat, saturates, sugars and salt to help consumers make healthier choices at a glance.

questions.q: What does a red section on a traffic light label indicate about a nutrient?
options: The food is low in that nutrient
The food is medium in that nutrient
The food is high in that nutrient
questions.explain: Red means the food is high in that nutrient and should be eaten only occasionally or in small amounts.

questions.q: What is meant by the term 'food miles'?
options: The distance food travels from where it is produced to where it is eaten
The number of shops selling a particular food
The energy value of a food in a portion
The distance a consumer walks around a supermarket
questions.explain: Food miles measure the distance food travels to reach the consumer and relate to its environmental impact.

questions.q: How does buying locally produced, seasonal food benefit the environment?
options: It increases the use of packaging
It reduces food miles and transport emissions
questions.explain: Local, seasonal food travels a shorter distance, reducing food miles and the emissions from transport and storage.

questions.q: What does the Fairtrade mark on a product tell the consumer?
options: Producers in developing countries received a fair, guaranteed price
The food is suitable for vegetarians
questions.explain: The Fairtrade mark shows that farmers and workers in developing countries were paid a fair and stable price.

questions.q: What does the Red Tractor logo assure the consumer about a food product?
options: It was produced to recognised UK safety, welfare and traceability standards
It is the cheapest option available
It was imported from outside the UK
questions.explain: The Red Tractor logo shows food has been produced, processed and packed to assured UK standards of safety, animal welfare and traceability.

questions.q: The blue MSC (Marine Stewardship Council) label on a fish product indicates that the fish was...
questions.explain: The MSC label certifies that fish comes from sustainable sources, helping protect fish stocks for the future.

questions.q: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, if food bought is of unsatisfactory quality, the consumer is entitled to...
options: Nothing, as food cannot be returned
A refund or replacement from the retailer
questions.explain: The retailer who sold the goods is responsible for putting things right, usually through a refund or replacement.

questions.q: A 500g box of branded cereal costs £2.50 and a 750g box of own-brand cereal costs £3.00. Which is better value and why?
options: Both are exactly the same value
questions.explain: The own-brand works out at 40p per 100g compared with 50p per 100g for the branded, so it is cheaper per unit weight.

questions.q: A 'buy one get one free' (BOGOF) offer on fresh yoghurts is only good value for a consumer if they...
options: Buy the most expensive brand available
Will use both packs before the use-by date
Store the extra pack for several months
Only need one pack that week
questions.explain: BOGOF offers only save money if the extra food is used before it spoils, otherwise it leads to waste and no saving.

questions.q: A shopper with a milk allergy wants to check whether a ready meal is safe. Where should they look on the label?
options: The ingredients list, where allergens are emphasised in bold
questions.explain: The 14 named allergens must be emphasised within the ingredients list, so a milk-allergic consumer can check there.

questions.q: A consumer wants the healthier of two ready meals using the traffic light labels. Which choice should they make?
options: The meal with the most red lights
The meal with more green and amber lights and fewer red lights
The meal with the highest energy value
The meal with no nutrition information shown
questions.explain: More greens and ambers with fewer reds indicates lower amounts of fat, saturates, sugars and salt, making it the healthier choice.
